rule: TS namespaces and named object literals (bound at the top level or exported) nest with dots (`mod.ns.f`, `mod.obj.f`); the object `module.exports`/`export default` is, is the module (`mod.f`); `module.exports = fn` is `mod.default`. | Anonymous functions, lambdas, object-literal methods and anonymous-class members fold into the nearest enclosing named function (or the module/type at top level). A caller is never empty. | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown". | **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding.
notes: `handlers` is a named object literal bound at the top level: its methods are `api.handlers.ping`/`api.handlers.echo`, and `handlers.ping()` resolves to that ID in its own file and in main.ts (C1). The `export default` object is the module, so `start` is `api.start`, and the default import `api.start()` resolves to it. The object literal returned inside `make` is anonymous: its method `run` folds into `api.make`, so `make().run()` is `.run` on a call result, low. call_type direct for object-literal members: their IDs are dotted like namespace functions, not `Type#m`; SPEC does not state call_type for them (see report).
